newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BANCOMER SAYS PESO TO STAY STRONG IF U.S. HEALTHY.
newsitem.headline: BANCOMER SAYS PESO TO STAY STRONG IF U.S. HEALTHY.

text.p: The chief executive of Mexico's Bancomer S.A., Ricardo Guajardo, said the peso would not be too badly affected by any U.S. interest rate rise so long as continued buoyancy of the U.S. economy helped Mexican exporters.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Guajardo said any U.S. interest rate rise "will accelerate the depreciation of the peso, but not much".
"The most important support for the peso lies in the strength of the U.S. economy. As long as that support continues, the peso will remain strong," he said.
Guajardo said he foresaw the peso would stand at 8.40 to 8.60 pesos per dollar by the end of 1997 (compared with a current rate of 7.90).

Asked how any onset of recession in the United States would hit Mexico, Guajardo said "if it happened tomorrow it would be a problem" but if it happened in 18 months to two years it would be "manageable" due to steps Mexico was taking to get its economy right.
He said the Mexican authorities were commited to maintaining good fiscal and monetary discipline and to allowing the peso to float.
He said his bank saw some signs of a pick-up in lending, with a mild increase in April in the number of credit card applications.
